cards.explanation: The answer is Moses. Moses, Israel's leader, is the one Paul means. The glory on his face was so strong that the Israelites could not gaze at it. Exodus 34:30 says they were afraid to come near him once they saw his face was radiant. That's a lot to carry around, friends, and he didn't even have a flashlight.

The answer is False. Paul says the glory on the face of Moses, Israel's leader, was a "fleeting glory." It was real and it was bright, but it was on its way out. Paul says the same thing again in verse 13, calling it "…what was fading away…"

The answer is True. Paul asks, "…will not the ministry of the Spirit be even more glorious?" He's building on the glory of the ministry of death and saying the ministry of the Spirit goes past it. He doesn't whisper it either, friends. He says it with his whole chest.

The answer is righteousness. Paul says that if the ministry of condemnation was glorious, "…how much more glorious is the ministry of righteousness!" Condemnation on one side, righteousness on the other. And Paul says the second one has the greater glory.

The answer is that it endures. Paul says what was fading away came with glory, and then he says, "…how much greater is the glory of that which endures!" One glory was fading, and the other lasts. That's the difference between a batch that cools off on the counter and a batch that stays warm.

The answer is True. Paul says, "…since we have such a hope, we are very bold." The hope comes first and the boldness follows. He doesn't say they're bold because they feel brave on a Monday morning, friends.

The answer is a veil. Paul says Moses "…would put a veil over his face…" Exodus 34:33 says the same, that Moses put a veil over his face. Paul brings it up because it connects to what he says next about the old covenant. A veil is simply a covering, friends, and that one went on his face.

The answer is so they wouldn't see the end of what was fading. Moses would put a veil over his face "…to keep the Israelites from gazing at the end of what was fading away." The glory on his face was fading, and the veil kept them from gazing at the end of it. I think that's a lot like covering a cookie tray with a towel so nobody watches the last of the steam rise. Paul gives the reason himself, so we can take it straight from him.

The answer is Christ. Paul says the veil "…has not been lifted, because only in Christ can it be removed." It's not removed by trying harder, and it's not removed by reading it again. He says it's only in Christ. My mustache can't lift that veil, friends, and neither can anyone else's.
The answer is hearts. Paul says, "…even to this day when Moses is read, a veil covers their hearts." He's not talking about a cloth on someone's face here. The covering is over their hearts.

The answer is whenever anyone turns to the Lord. Paul says, "…whenever anyone turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away." Notice the word "anyone." He doesn't set a limit on who can turn. And when someone turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.

The answer is freedom. Paul says the veil is taken away whenever anyone turns to the Lord, and then he says, "…where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom." Where the Spirit of the Lord is, there's freedom. That's a good place to stand, friends.

The answer is that we are being transformed into His image. Paul says those of us who reflect the glory of the Lord with unveiled faces "…are being transformed into His image with intensifying glory…" Notice it's "are being." It's happening now, and it keeps going. And he says the glory comes from the Lord, who is the Spirit.

The answer is False. The fading belongs to the glory on Moses' face. Paul says we "…are being transformed into His image with intensifying glory, which comes from the Lord, who is the Spirit." It's an intensifying glory, friends, so it grows instead of fading.
